brief: GS Sales & Trading's weekly positioning note: the Global Equities prime-brokerage book sold at a 2-standard-deviation pace last week, pushing fundamental long/short net leverage to the 1st percentile of its 5-year range. Info Tech was by far the most net-sold global sector, with the sharpest percentage de-grossing in 2 months and the largest percentage net selling on record since 2016; 8 of 11 global sectors were net sold overall. Retail and fund flows took the other side: global equity funds drew +$65bn in net inflows (versus +$12bn the prior week), led by US technology funds, even as the SOX semiconductor index had its worst week this year (-11%) and nearly $10bn poured into levered ETFs, with SOXL (3x semis) gathering a record +$7bn. The retail bid itself wavered, though, with the SPX retail imbalance turning negative for the first time since July on Friday. CTA models had been forecasting buying into the weekend, but the desk says that is probably invalidated now that the S&P broke below its short-term threshold. Corporates stay subdued buyers until November, when the bid is expected to return in force.
